defaults.commit_style: test: realign static gates to current editor canon

tasks.title: Realign 4 stale editor static gates to current canon (hotfix for CI Parity Check)
steps: These 4 gates run in CI via plain `node <file>` and FAIL after the L2M/L2N waves changed the editor. Update the ASSERTIONS (not the editor) — the editor is canonical now:

(a) nonbreaking-hyphen.test.mjs asserts 'Ctrl+Minus (no Shift) must emit an en dash with preventDefault' — OBSOLETE canon. Current canon (L2M-05): en-dash is Control+Hyphen (ev.code 'Hyphen'), plain Control+Minus calls zoomOut(), Control+Shift+Minus inserts nonbreaking hyphen if that was the old secondary. READ editor.js keydown handler (grep Hyphen / Minus / zoomOut / en dash) and rewrite the gate's assertions to the real current bindings. Rename assertions/messages to match.

(b) ctx-edit-wrap-boundary.test.mjs: 'index.html: EditWrapBoundary row must sit inside the ctx wrap block' — inspect the current ctx menu wrap block in index.html (grep EditWrapBoundary, TopAndBottom, data-ctx="Rotate90") and realign the structural assertion to where the row actually sits now (L2M-03 added Rotate90/TopAndBottom rows).

(c) ctx-through.test.mjs + ctx-tight.test.mjs: 'editor.js: applyObjectOp wrap branch must accept wrap-through / wrap-tight' — check the actual applyObjectOp branch (grep wrap-through / wrap-top-and-bottom) and update the assertion text/values to the current accepted set (wrap-top-and-bottom was ADDED).

Verify each gate exits 0: for f in ctx-edit-wrap-boundary ctx-through ctx-tight nonbreaking-hyphen; do /usr/bin/node apps/.../$f.test.mjs || exit 1; done (run from apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg). Also confirm the WHOLE suite: for f in *.test.mjs; do /usr/bin/node "$f" >/dev/null || echo FAIL: $f; done — expect no output (this exact loop is the CI gate).
Commit ONLY the four listed files.
tasks.accept: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/apps/web/apps/documenteditor-wysiwyg" && fails=0; for f in *.test.mjs; do /usr/bin/node "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fails=$((fails+1)); done; test "$fails" -eq 0
